chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sukuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) said:
(There are) two strange things, so bear with them: a word of wisdom from a fool, so accept it; and a word of foolishness from a wise man, so forgive it.
ai.seo_question: What are the two strange things one must expect according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, highlights the Shia emphasis on discerning truth from its source rather than being swayed by social status or eloquence. It serves as a practical guide for intellectual humility, urging believers to accept wisdom even from the 'foolish' (safihi) and overlook errors from the 'wise' (hakim), reflecting the nuanced understanding of *hikmah* in Shia scholarship.
